questions.q: Maya Ortiz closed $420K against a $375K quarterly quota. What is her attainment?
Why does the lesson add a joined report with an open-pipeline block next to Closed Won?
options: Attainment looks backward; open pipeline shows whether each rep can still close their gap
Joined reports are the only way to sort by owner
It removes the need for a quota
questions.explain: Pairing closed revenue with open pipeline lets you compare what is left to win against what is available to win it.

questions.q: Why can a summary formula like AMOUNT:SUM / 375000 hard-code the quota in this project?
options: Salesforce does not allow any other quota to be stored
Because every rep has the same $375K quarterly quota; if quotas differed you would use a bucket column or forecast quotas
Because quotas are always $375K in every org
Because the formula ignores the owner
questions.explain: Hard-coding is only acceptable when the quota is identical for every rep in the report.

questions.q: Tomas Silva has the largest average deal ($50K) but the lowest attainment (40%). What does this suggest?
options: His deals are too large, so he should sell smaller ones
Deal count and pipeline volume, not deal size, is the likelier issue (only 3 deals)
He has no open pipeline at all
questions.explain: With only three closed deals, the shortfall points to volume, not to the size of each deal.

questions.q: What is the responsible way to present rep-level performance?
options: As a public leaderboard of blame
Without any context, so the numbers speak for themselves
Emailing raw data to every employee
As a coaching view with context (territory, timing, ramp), and only to people entitled to see it
questions.explain: Attainment reflects more than skill, and per-rep visibility should follow the company's sharing rules.
